concept.name: Composite operator
concept.definition: Wyckoff's heuristic device of treating all market fluctuations as if they were produced by one fictional large operator, the Composite Man, who plans, executes, and concludes campaigns of accumulation and distribution. It is a mental model for interpreting chart behavior, not the claim that a single entity actually controls prices.
concept.intuition: Pretend the whole market is one clever dealer running a shop: it builds inventory quietly, advertises to attract buyers at high prices, then sells out before prices fall.
concept.mechanics: The analyst studies each chart as the Composite Man's campaign, judging from price, volume, and time whether the operator is accumulating, distributing, or marking prices up or down, and aligns trades with the inferred stage of that campaign. Wyckoff taught that the operator attracts public participation by creating the appearance of a broad, active market.
concept.failure_modes: The anthropomorphic model invites confirmation bias: almost any price path can be rationalized as operator intent, and modern markets with many competing institutions, index funds, and algorithms fit the single-operator picture poorly.
concept.misconceptions: Wyckoff did not claim markets are literally manipulated by one cabal; he explicitly said it does not matter whether moves are 'real or artificial', only that the trader understands the game being played.
concept.example: A trader interprets a stock's quiet sideways drift on shrinking volume after a panic low as the Composite Man absorbing supply, then treats a high-volume breakout as the start of the operator's markup campaign.

citations.source: The Wyckoff Method: A Tutorial (StockCharts.com ChartSchool, by Roman Bogomazov and Michael Lipsett)
